attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet point in his own post, written in his voice.

semantics.note: An unqualified 'Expect' is a scored forecast. The threshold 'a lot' and the horizon 'in the coming years' are both kept.

contract.note: Reading 'a lot' in absolute terms (tens of thousands of complaints, hundreds of millions in losses) is an ordinary reading. The ~2% relative share is a known caveat, but the speaker named no relative measure.

evidence.note: FBI 2025 IC3 report, available April 2026: 22,364 AI-related complaints and about $893M in losses. This meets the early-resolution thresholds.
AI-lab threat report on a confirmed large extortion operation run with Claude Code in 2025. It is a company disclosure but also a primary threat report, which the contract allows.
A qualitative finding that AI lowers the barriers to cybercrime. It gives no count of scale, so it does not measure the outcome by itself.

reviews.rationale: The FBI's official 2025 figures (22,364 AI-related complaints, about $893M in losses) meet the contract's early-resolution rule, which asks for tens of thousands of complaints or hundreds of millions in losses. Anthropic's report adds confirmed large operations. The low relative share and the victim-reported attribution are caveats, but nothing contradicts the outcome.

attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet point in his own post.

semantics.note: Reading this as a claim about AI regulation fits the context. It is an observation about the period up to December 2024.

contract.note: The plain reading (no substantial federal AI regulation, plus wins or influence for the anti-regulation camp in 2023–24) is ordinary and fair to the loose wording.

evidence.note: Law-firm tracker: the NDAA (December 18, after the post) held the first and likely only AI provisions of the 118th Congress.
The NDAA's AI provisions are defense pilots, not general AI regulation.
A deregulatory investor, David Sacks, was named AI czar on December 5, 2024: a gain in influence for the anti-regulation camp.
SB 1047, which a16z lobbied against, was vetoed in September 2024: a policy win for Andreessen's side.

reviews.rationale: Congress passed no general AI regulation in 2023–24; its only AI provisions were defense-focused NDAA items passed after the post. Anti-regulation figures gained ground: SB 1047 was vetoed after a16z lobbying, and Sacks was appointed AI czar. Both parts hold.
